papers.title: WAIT-A-SEC: A Human-Centered Design Approach to Privacy Communication for Social Media Oversharing
papers.abstract: Social media platforms often operate on extractive security logics that prioritize frictionless data sharing, leaving users disempowered and prone to oversharing sensitive information, without fully recognizing the associated privacy implications. We present WAIT-A-SEC (Warnings About Information Transfer And Sharing: Encouraging Caution), hereafter referred to as WAITASEC, an interactive proof-of-concept prototype that delivers real-time privacy alerts while users compose posts to minimize instances of oversharing. Leveraging a synthetic dataset of 90 annotated examples of realistic user-generated content, our evaluations compare three separate models 1) a rule-based regular expressions (regex) and named entity recognition (NER) through spaCy, 2) a large language model (LLM) and 3) a hybrid model that combines the previous two models as well as incorporates a knowledge graph (KG) and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to provide context. In this hybrid approach, regex and NER yield candidate classifications, which are then validated and expanded by the LLM, utilizing RAG to retrieve relevant context from the KG before sending feedback back to the user. This classifier achieves optimal performance (Macro-F1 = 0.897; Micro-F1 = 0.834), significantly reducing critical false negatives. Grounded in Technical and Professional Communication (TPC) and active learning principles, we advocate for a warning-first design that introduces intentional pedagogical friction. This tactical approach promotes user reflection and fosters enduring privacy literacy, restoring user agency rather than relying on passive, automated redaction. This paper concludes with deployment considerations and next steps for user studies.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Online hydrodynamic parameter identification for an ROV using an enhanced physics-informed neural network

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文用物理信息神经网络在线辨识ROV水动力参数，方法可迁移到FEA代理建模与参数反演，但应用领域为海洋机器人而非生物力学。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate for solid mechanics, no biomedical or implant context, and no uncertainty quantification; it targets online hydrodynamic parameter identification for an underwater vehicle.

summary_zh.motivation: 水下机器人水动力参数难以在线准确获取，影响控制精度。
summary_zh.method: 构建增强型物理信息神经网络，将动力学方程嵌入损失函数实现在线参数辨识。
summary_zh.result: 在仿真工况下实现水动力系数的在线估计并提升辨识精度。
summary_zh.validation: 基于ROV动力学仿真案例进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Accurate online identification of hydrodynamic parameters is essential for reliable control of remotely operated vehicles.
summary_en.method: An enhanced physics-informed neural network embeds the vehicle dynamics equations into the training loss to identify hydrodynamic coefficients online.
summary_en.result: The approach estimates hydrodynamic parameters online with improved identification accuracy in simulated operating conditions.
summary_en.validation: The method is assessed through simulation case studies of an ROV dynamics model.

papers.title: Fe₃O₄–CNT/paraffin nanoparticles impact on MHD Darcy–Forchheimer flow heat transfer using physics-informed neural network

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文用PINN求解磁流体多孔介质传热问题，与FEA代理建模方向仅有PINN方法层面的弱关联，不涉及生物力学或植入体设计。
llm.why_not_core: It applies PINN to a magnetohydrodynamic Darcy–Forchheimer nanofluid heat transfer problem with no solid-mechanics FEA, no implant/biomechanics context, no surrogate-based design optimization, and no uncertainty quantification.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索PINN在复杂磁流体多孔介质传热问题中的求解能力。
summary_zh.method: 构建PINN求解Fe₃O₄–CNT/石蜡纳米流体的MHD Darcy–Forchheimer流动与传热方程。
summary_zh.result: PINN预测与数值参考解吻合，验证了其在耦合多物理场问题上的可行性。
summary_zh.validation: 与数值求解结果对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to assess whether physics-informed neural networks can efficiently solve coupled magnetohydrodynamic heat transfer in nanofluid-saturated porous media.
summary_en.method: A PINN framework is trained to satisfy the governing MHD Darcy–Forchheimer flow and energy equations for Fe₃O₄–CNT/paraffin nanofluid.
summary_en.result: The network reproduces the reference velocity and temperature fields with good agreement, indicating feasibility for coupled multiphysics problems.
summary_en.validation: Predictions are compared against conventional numerical solutions of the same governing equations.

papers.title: Study on Pneumatic Flow Control Algorithm Based on Physics-Informed Bayesian Optimization for Flow Cytometry
papers.venue: Journal of the korean society of manufacturing technology engineers

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文将物理信息贝叶斯优化用于流式细胞术气动流控，方法学上可迁移到FEA代理模型的采样与优化，但应用领域与植入物/生物力学无关。
llm.why_not_core: It applies physics-informed Bayesian optimization to pneumatic flow control in flow cytometry, with no FEA surrogate modeling, no implant mechanics, and no biomechanical design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 流式细胞术气动流控参数调节依赖昂贵仿真与试错。
summary_zh.method: 构建物理信息贝叶斯优化框架，融合物理约束引导气动流控参数搜索。
summary_zh.result: 在流控场景下提升优化效率并给出不确定性感知的参数选择。
summary_zh.validation: 基于流控仿真案例进行数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: Tuning pneumatic flow parameters in flow cytometry is costly and relies on expensive simulation or trial-and-error.
summary_en.method: A physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework is constructed to guide the search over pneumatic flow control parameters under physical constraints.
summary_en.result: The approach improves optimization efficiency and yields uncertainty-aware parameter selections in the flow control scenario.
summary_en.validation: Numerical validation is performed on simulation cases of the flow control system.

papers.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the gameful experience scale (GAMEX) for Brazil
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Gamification has emerged as an innovative teaching methodology, particularly in nursing education, fostering engagement and active learning. Objective To translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Gameful Experience Scale (GAMEX) for Brazilian Portuguese. Methods A methodological, quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted in three phases: linguistic and cultural adaptation, content validation, and construct validation. The cross-cultural adaptation followed World Health Organization guidance and the six-stage process described by Beaton et al.: forward translation, synthesis, back translation, expert committee review, pre-testing, and documentation of the final version. Content equivalence was assessed through expert committee review and pre-testing with representatives of the target population. Construct validity was examined using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with a diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS) estimator and polychoric correlations, and reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega. Discriminant validity was examined using the average variance extracted (AVE), the Fornell-Larcker criterion, and the heterotrait-monotrait ratio (HTMT). Results A total of 135 participants were included in the validation sample, with a mean age of 30.1 ± 13.1 years (range: 17–67 years). The sample comprised 82 students (60.7%) and 53 professionals (39.3%) from the nursing school setting. The Brazilian Portuguese adaptation demonstrated promising psychometric performance. Domain reliability levels were as follows: Enjoyment (α = 0.911; ω = 0.910), Absorption (α = 0.917; ω = 0.917), Creative Thinking (α = 0.866; ω = 0.869), Activation (α = 0.657; ω = 0.556), Absence of Negative Affect (α = 0.852; ω = 0.856), and Dominance (α = 0.770; ω = 0.770). CFA supported the overall six-factor structure, with χ² = 581.706, df = 309, χ²/df = 1.883, CFI = 0.958, TLI = 0.953, RMSEA = 0.081 (90% CI: 0.071–0.091), and SRMR = 0.102. However, RMSEA and SRMR were marginally above the prespecified thresholds, and the Activation domain showed weaker psychometric performance. Items Q18 and Q19 require further linguistic, experiential, and psychometric refinement. Conclusions The Brazilian Portuguese adaptation of GAMEX showed promising evidence of structural validity and internal consistency for assessing gamified learning experiences, such as escape rooms, in this nursing education sample.

llm.why_not_core: This is a psychometric scale translation/validation study in nursing education with no simulation, surrogate modeling, optimization, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics content.

summary_zh.motivation: 为巴西葡萄牙语护理教育提供游戏化体验测量工具。
summary_zh.method: 按WHO与Beaton流程翻译量表，并用验证性因子分析检验结构效度。
summary_zh.result: 六因子结构基本成立，但激活维度与个别条目心理测量表现较弱。
summary_zh.validation: 135名护理学生与从业者的横断面问卷数据。

summary_en.motivation: The study aimed to make the Gameful Experience Scale available and psychometrically sound for Brazilian Portuguese nursing education contexts.
summary_en.method: The scale was translated and culturally adapted following WHO and Beaton guidelines, then construct validity was assessed via confirmatory factor analysis with DWLS estimation and reliability indices.
summary_en.result: The six-factor structure was broadly supported with acceptable reliability, although the Activation domain and two items showed weaker psychometric performance and some fit indices marginally exceeded thresholds.
summary_en.validation: Cross-sectional survey data from 135 nursing students and professionals were used for psychometric validation.
